text: TAVRIN VALLEY, Nov. 13 — Barley failed across the Tavrin Valley this season after weeks of erratic frost and a late blight, according to people familiar with the matter. The harvest gap was first flagged in early October by agronomists at the Halden Field Station, who said yields in the lowland plots fell to near zero, while neighboring rye and oat plantings held up better. Local cooperatives had expected roughly 18,000 metric tons of barley, but revised estimates now put output at less than a fifth of that figure. Farmers in the valley’s eastern ring have already begun replanting winter feed, the people said.
